claim: Hard-coding sender names in conversation-handling rules requires rewriting all rules when the scenario is altered, reducing extensibility.
falsifier: Implement a multi-agent protocol with hard-coded sender names and measure the effort required to adapt it to a new scenario with different agents.

conditions: observed in participant implementations in an asset trading game experiment
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, population, and conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Hard-coding sender names for extensibility of the rule

claim: Domain-specific post-training instills robust zero-shot capabilities and raises the performance ceiling for downstream fine-tuning on the same domain.
falsifier: Take a base LLM, apply domain-specific post-training, then fine-tune on a downstream task in the same domain; compare zero-shot performance and fine-tuned performance against a model without domain-specific post-training.

conditions: downstream fine-tuning uses the same domain
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system (FitOne models based on Qwen3), task (SFC certification exams), and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.
